g.text: : The test that would not pass
It is past midnight and the EOW is empty except for you and the hum of LANTERN. The eval results are
open on the screen. You have fixed prompts all evening, and the pass rate has climbed. One test has not
moved. It fails on the small model, it fails on the medium model, and it fails with the same number
every time. You stop trying to fix the prompt and start reading the evidence.
. Start with the headline, then distrust it
. A single number hides which tests, which models and which prompts.
. Break it down: which assertion failed, where
. Compare prompts on the same tests
Same model, same tests, different prompt: the gap between v1 and v2 is the prompt's work.
. Group failures by test: what fails everywhere, and how?
Some cells: a prompt or a model problem. Every cell with different answers: the task is hard, or the gold
label is debatable. Every cell with the SAME answer: suspect the expected value.
The four threats that fail everywhere are the quiet ones
is a human judgement, made with context the model does not have.
. Read one failure in full: extract NW-
Bill to: Halcyon Maritime Logistics, Pier 9 Administration, Kestrel Bay
Remit to: Account 88-301-4471, Sabran Mercantile Bank
date=2026-03-03, payee=Northwind Freight Ltd, description=Freight coordination services, March lot
from the invoice. The models are right. The test expects the ledger, and the
. Bad prompt, bad test, or bad data?
Not a bad prompt: both models give the same total, and it matches the document.
Not a bad assertion: the code compares numbers correctly; every other invoice passes.
Bad data: the reference record itself disagrees with its source. Ask why.
2026-03-31 09:12:04,a.varma,ingest,EX-014 ledger.csv,seized from Halcyon finance server; sha256
2026-03-31 09:14:40,a.varma,ingest,EX-015 invoices/,8 files from T. Reyes mailbox export; sha256
2026-04-03 02:47:36,pk.dsouza,modify,EX-014 ledger.csv,row reference NW-0419; field amount_kbd; sha256 now
: Detective Sergeant P. K. D'Souza changed row NW-0419, field amount_kbd in
: The account of PK. D'Souza is marked as disabled in the HR system, and it was
. Check LANTERN against the log, line by line
LANTERN's timestamp does not match that line.
It took a time from a neighbouring row. Quote-checking catches
An account is not a person. The log shows the pk.dsouza login was used. It does not show who typed the
password. LANTERN's wording blurs that; your report must not.
The ledger was seized on 31 March. At 02:47 on 3 April, an account called pk.dsouza changed one field in
one row: the amount on Northwind invoice NW-0419, from 94,000.00 to 9,400.00. The account belongs to a
detective sergeant who retired three years ago. It had not been used since. Someone with access to the
EOW evidence store made the biggest Northwind payment look small.
Case File 01 is closed with its question answered. Tomas Reyes did not fall by accident. At 23:36
someone opened the bottom door of stairwell C from the outside, using an audit override code that
Brightwater and Co had been given and never handed back. Raj Malhotra's sixteen minutes do not add up.
Three invoices paid a company with no ships into an account in Port Sabran.
Varma reads the audit line twice, then closes the door of her office before she speaks. "Nobody outside
this room hears about this. Not the duty sergeant, not headquarters. Tomorrow we start on the archive:
twenty years of Halcyon's records, and every one of them has been in a building that someone inside this
Case File 02 begins in the archive.
